items.title: Making sense of the latest GOP attack on corporate climate action
items.summary: The accusations come in a Aug. 24 letter from Nebraska AG Mike Hilgers and allies that is notable both for bringing a new batch of companies into the campaign and for the legal arguments it contains, which differ from those used in recent campaigns against climate nonprofits.

items.title: A $450bn challenge: What do rising climate catastrophe losses mean?
items.summary: Natural disasters now cost the world around $450bn a year and only 38% of that is insured. Here, edie breaks down how and why the climate risk bill is growing, and where blind spots remain.

items.title: NEXT WEEK: Exploring the role of bio-based materials in lower-carbon buildings
items.summary: Next week, edie is hosting a new webinar exploring the growing interest in bio-based materials.

items.title: Onshore wind farms could save UK £3bn a year by 2030
items.summary: As Europe looks on track for a record year of wind deployment, new analysis has estimated that UK taxpayers could save £3bn a year if the country meets its 2030 target for onshore wind.

items.title: The new NPPF: Good growth needs multi-use land
items.summary: With demand growing for new homes, renewable energy, infrastructure and nature restoration, chief executive of the Chartered Institute of Ecology and Environmental Management (CIEEM), Sally Hayns, argues that the latest planning reforms should have done more to ensure the country's land delivers multiple benefits.

items.title: From sustainability to security: Are PPAs becoming a risk mitigation tool?
items.summary: With compliance expected to push businesses towards hourly and local-based energy reporting, many organisations are exploring shorter-length contracts that protect them from ongoing price volatility.

items.title: Report: Fashion industry emissions rise 14% in two years
items.summary: A new report from Apparel Impact Institute (Aii) has estimated that emissions from the fashion sector rose for the second year in a row in 2024, bringing its carbon footprint up 13.8% in two years.

items.title: TWO WEEKS to go until edie’s Sustainable Supply Chains Summit
items.summary: Join us on 17 September for a unique opportunity to gain expert-led insights through thought leadership and industry panels featuring top professionals in sustainability, supply chain and procurement.

items.title: Guest post: Why tough methane cuts are crucial for keeping warming ‘well-below’ 2C
items.summary: Methane is a powerful greenhouse gas and the second-largest contributor to global warming after carbon dioxide (CO2).
